title: Countdown: 3 faces per digit, and no re-rendering while nobody can see it
problem: The countdown clock re-renders its rolling digits on every animation frame, even when it can't be seen: the hero clock after it fades out or scrolls away, and the second clock in the morph panel, which sits at opacity 0 for most of the page. Each digit is 10 stacked faces. On the full page in Chrome, past the hero, the main thread was busy about 760-815 ms less per 6 s with the change below (n=1, Chrome at 6x CPU, a CPU profile, not a timing A/B). In the iOS Simulator the hidden clocks cause about 100 extra layouts and 100 extra paints per 4 s past the hero (n=1, Simulator, not the phone).
idea: Follow apple.com's pattern (iPhone page, media-card gallery): animations play only while their scroll range is on screen, the page decides this from the scroll position, and only the cards next to the visible one are rendered. One difference: a countdown must show the current time, so on return it shows the frame an always-running clock shows, instead of continuing from where it stopped.
looksSame: Checked with frozen frames in Chrome on the hero clock: the countdown's clock and frames are virtual and stepped identically in both versions, with frame times jittered by up to 1 ms like real ones and the 1-second tick falling mid-frame. 295 screenshots were compared byte for byte, plus the exact position of every visible face: rest, every phase of 6 kinds of roll at 60 Hz and 4 kinds at 120 Hz, and coming back after a fade-out, after scrolling away, after a tab switch and after two ticks while away. 0 of 295 differ; the baseline against itself also gives 0. The first frame after an instant jump back was read in 12 cases: 0 differ. Not shot: the panel clock, Safari/WebKit, a real 120 Hz screen.
risk: This replaces the earlier countdown fix #1 (countdown-idle-raf) in the same code: #1 snaps a hidden clock, which shows a different digit when the clock comes back mid-roll. The panel call site is shared with the morph lazy-mount fix (#13); when both land, the panel uses the stricter visibility condition. With hidden frames cheaper, Chrome at 6x renders more frames, so total style recalcs and paints for the page rise 10-25 % (less per frame). At the faded-out hero, layouts are +7 % and paints +13 %, cause unknown (n=3). While the clock is visible, about 1 small layout and 2 face repaints per second are added (a face slot changes its digit once per roll). The saving ends when the countdown expires (2026-11-02 05:00 UTC). Safari was checked for counts in the Simulator only; a phone check is needed before landing. No timing gain is claimed.

options.name: full
options.label: 3 faces + no re-rendering while unseen
options.idea: Each digit keeps 3 face slots instead of 10 (the two that can be in view plus one spare). While the clock is faded out, scrolled away or in the hidden panel, its spring keeps counting in the background but nothing is re-rendered; in the frame the clock is shown again it displays the value the original computes for the same frames. The hidden clock's spring still runs on every animation frame (about as many frames as today); only the re-rendering is skipped.
options.looksSame: Pixel-identical in Chrome in all 295 frozen-frame shots (142 rolls, 153 coming back) and in the first frame after 12 instant jumps back. The conditions: the hero clock, 60 and 120 Hz virtual frames. Not shot: the panel clock, Safari, real 120 Hz screens.
options.risk: Touches the hero's fade-out code and the panel call site (shared with #13); replaces fix #1's version of the same code.
visualDiff: Nothing visible in the shots: 0 of 295 frozen frames differ, at rest, mid-roll and on coming back, including the first frame after a jump.
